title: Suncrest Commerce — post-demo capture
body:
Meeting: Suncrest Commerce — post-demo quick capture (2026-03-05)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Redwood Solutions), Lina Romero (Suncrest, Eng Lead), Ben Park (Suncrest, Infra)
Purpose: rapid recap after demo + surface technical requirements/risks so SEs/SREs can size a POC and next steps.

1) Demo recap (what landed / reactions)
- Showed hosted API latency profile for retail search rerank + conversational product assistant. Lina liked streaming response demo and token-level cost view.
- Ben: primary concern is customer data flow and ensuring no PII leaves VPC. Liked Private option but asked about effort.
- They were surprised by the 95p90/95 latency numbers for short queries — motivated by predictable latency.

2) High-level business requirements (from Lina/Ben)
- Blackbox requirement: all customer product catalog + user session data must remain inside their GCP VPC (no export to hosted model store).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 120ms for generation path for product lookup / autocomplete (typical token length ~8); conversational flows can accept up to 400ms at 95p if batched.
- Throughput expectations: peak 150 TPS for rerank endpoint during promotions (10x baseline), baseline 15 TPS.
- Compliance: PCI + regional data residency (EU customer subset must stay in eu-west1), audit logs required for all inference requests.
- Budget: target monthly inference spend <$12k for POC (approx token/embedding mix to estimate later).

3) Technical details & constraints (notes to team)
- Target deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) preferred; consider a Dedicated reserved pool only if Private onboarding timeline is too long.
- Models: start with opt-in open LLM (e.g., an Llama-2-like quantized variant) for retrieval-augmented reranking; consider a smaller distilled chat model for assistant. Must validate model licensing for PCI-scope data.
- Sequence lengths: product description prompts average 40–120 tokens; some sessions produce up to 800 tokens (rare). This affects kv-cache pressure and memory planning.
- KV cache warmup: helpful to prewarm common prefixes (product SKUs) during promo windows. Ask data team for top-5k SKUs to seed cache.
- Batching: continuous batching acceptable for rerank if latency SLOs are met; use dynamic max-batch-size with strict latency cap.
- Quantization: Suncrest pushes for int8 to reduce GPU memory; we need to verify model accuracy/regression on their prompt set. Redwood Optimize suggestions will be useful here.

4) Integration gotchas surfaced during call
- Mobile clients sometimes send full session transcript leading to large sequence lengths — need a pre-filter on client to truncate or send summarized context. Put this as a mitigatable risk.
- Rate-limiting: their client SDK retries aggressively on 5xx which amplified a brief failure into a traffic spike in demo. Propose seat-based quotas + client backoff guidance.
- Embedding storage: they want embeddings stored in their managed vector store (Pinecone-like) inside EU for EU customers — ensure we can route embedding generation within region and not replicate to hosted tooling.
- Logging/audit: They require redaction rules for PII before logs leave host. Need mapping of Redwood's audit pipeline to their KMS/HSM approach.
- Model fallback: they asked about graceful degradation to smaller models during saturation — ensure routing policies include fallback variants and cost tiering.

5) Data & security follow-ups (action items for security/compliance)
- Lina to share a short list of data categories (PII vs non-PII) and sample payloads (anonymized) by EOD 2026-03-09.
- SRE/Security: we need to produce an integration note describing network topology for Private: control plane endpoints, data plane egress rules, and KMS integration points. (Owner: Jordan)
- Compliance: map Redwood audit log format to their SOC2 / PCI log ingestion expectations. Identify gaps. (Owner: Maya)

6) Capacity & cost sizing quick notes
- Estimate tokens: baseline day ~2M tokens (generation + embeddings) — big uncertainty here; ask them for daily query volume sample.
- GPU selection: for quantized LLM with 8-bit, consider A10G / H100x small cluster (depending on model size). For POC prefer 1x A100/80GB equivalent to reduce warmup friction.
- Dedicated vs Private sizing: if we go Private in their VPC, we should plan for min headroom of 2x peak (so reserve for 300 TPS short-burst capability).

7) Open questions (requires answers before POC scope finalization)
- Can Suncrest share a 48–72h traffic trace (anonymized) to calibrate batching and tail latencies?
- Do they have a preferred vector DB vendor or will they evaluate multiple? Any access constraints to connect from Private cluster?
- Exact retention policy for request/response logs and who controls purge: Redwood or Suncrest?
- Any encryption-at-rest keys they mandate be customer-managed (HSM) for model caches / KV?

8) Immediate next steps (owner + ETA)
- Jordan: produce Private deployment topology doc + rough onboarding checklist (ETA: 2026-03-12).
- Maya: create a sample token-cost estimate spreadsheet using three traffic scenarios (low/median/promo) and share (ETA: 2026-03-11).
- Lina/Ben: deliver anonymized sample payloads + top-5k SKU list (ETA: 2026-03-09).
- Set technical deep-dive session with Suncrest infra + security (90m) to walk through VPC peering, firewall rules, KMS. (Target week of 2026-03-15) — Maya to schedule.

9) Quick prompts / evals we want from them for model validation
- 25 deterministic rerank prompts with expected ordering (helpful for regression testing).
- 10 conversational flows with expected intents and acceptance criteria (latency/quality tradeoffs).

10) Misc notes / random capture (notes to self)
- Consider building a small client-side SDK snippet to prevent full-session sends from mobile (truncate/summarize). Could drop into onboarding docs.
- Remind: check whether Redwood Optimize can provide auto-quant suggestion for their SKU-heavy prompts.
- Potential commercial ask: trial dedicated capacity discount if they commit to 6mo. Mark as possible negotiation point.

End — keep this doc as working notes until we have the traffic sample and topology doc; will convert to more formal POC brief once missing artifacts arrive.

Raw timestamps: 2026-03-05 11:05 PST — call end.
summary: Post-demo working notes for Suncrest Commerce POC: Private deployment preferred; key constraints: VPC-only data, PCI & EU data residency, latency SLOs 95p < 120ms for short paths, 150 TPS promo peak. Action owners: Jordan (topology), Maya (costs), Suncrest (payloads + SKU list). Open: traffic trace, embedding storage routing, KMS ownership. Schedule 90m deep-dive week of 2026-03-15.
